intended_object: A one-field wrapper around `Scheme.{u}`, so that the type can carry a second `Category` instance: the category whose objects are schemes and whose morphisms are rational maps that pull back dense opens to dense opens. Inferred from the docstring and the module docs.
explanation: The structure has a single field, `toScheme : Scheme.{u}`. It adds no condition or data. It exists only so that a new type can be given a `Category` instance different from Mathlib's usual category of schemes and morphisms. In that new category the arrows are `Scheme.RationalMap`s satisfying `PullsDenseOpens`, and composition is `compOfPullsDenseOpens`. The wrapper is the standard Lean/Mathlib trick of a type synonym or one-field structure for carrying a different instance; compare `Opposite` or `Under`-style wrappers. Mathematically it stands for "a scheme": every scheme is allowed and nothing is restricted. So it is an implementation device, not a mathematical object in its own right. The mathematical content sits in the `Hom` structure and the `Category` instance, not in this declaration.
